rapport_notes: Warm opening and closing, friendly tone, but mostly silent acknowledgment throughout the call; limited personality or engagement beyond procedural exchanges.
process_discipline_notes: Calvin did not hold silence after the estimate explanation ('Does that all make sense')—customer said 'Sure' and he immediately pivoted to more details instead of waiting.

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Calvin: 'I was giving you a call. It looks like you got a move coming up for Monday September 21st did you have like 1015 minutes to go through that?' — frames the ask (10–15 minutes) but does not promise an accurate quote in return or set clear context for the benefit.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Calvin launched directly into item-by-item logistics ('are we gonna need to pack any boxes') without asking 'What are your biggest concerns about this move?' or equivalent.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised a concern about a person refusing to leave the house post-sale and the need for security. Calvin said 'Okay, I guess yeah that's kind of a concern but yeah, we can work with that' and immediately pivoted to packing questions with no follow-up on the concern itself.
evidence_quotes.sheet1_careful_with: Never mentioned. No 'What items do you need us to be most careful with?' or damage-coverage discussion anywhere in the call.
evidence_quotes.sheet2_whos_coming: Never mentioned. No 'Who's actually showing up?' / Meet Your Mover answer anywhere.
evidence_quotes.communication: Never mentioned anywhere (no day-before call, named crew lead, or inbox updates).
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Calvin: 'I was gonna say, you're probably looking in the range of about five to six hours, but again, you do only pay for what's used. But yeah, they'll probably put you in a cost, strange of around like, $945 to about $1,300 or so.' — gives a range and alludes to packing/elevator time as personalizing factors, but does not explicitly name the typical baseline or connect the range to the customer's specific logistics in a structured way.
evidence_quotes.estimate_is_a_window: Calvin: 'you do only pay for what's used' and 'you only pay for the time that you need the guys for' — implies the estimate can vary, but does not name specific factors (e.g., 'your move is yours because of X, Y, Z') that could cause the time to shift.
evidence_quotes.beats_it_pay_less: Calvin: 'Once we exceed the minimum we just bill in fifteen minute increments until the move is completed. So you would just pay for the time that you need the guys for.' — covered in the mechanics explanation; close to the intent but not framed as a win ('If the crew beats it, you pay less').
evidence_quotes.close_explicit_ask: Calvin: 'Did you wanna get that on the calendar?' — explicit ask, customer said 'Absolutely. Yeah, I love it. Let's, let's go for it.'

top_strength: Calvin successfully gathered detailed inventory information and moved smoothly into pricing and booking without getting lost in the logistics; the customer felt heard and booked immediately.
coaching_note: Ask 'What are your biggest concerns about this move, and what do you want answers to on this call?' before any probing—this is the critical missing line that would have surfaced the security concern early and positioned you to answer it with differentiators; also deliver the four core differentiators (damage coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, Communication) either organically as Stage 1 answers or as a deliberate Stage 2 takeaway to earn trust and separation.
